what: Source images were screened by pose/attribute/InsightFace proxy, not human visual review.
why: The executor cannot see images. source_review.png remains available for a human check.
impact: Formal identities could still contain an image a human would reject.

what: The 176-task single-rater blind review is complete.
why: Human visual judgment cannot be automated honestly.
impact: Human columns come from the corrected 160-original/16-repeat analysis; one rater only.

what: The SD2.1-base snapshot is the fp16-only sd2-community mirror already used by the old project.
why: It is the frozen weight set bound by the protocol; SHA256 hashes are in assets/pretrained hashes.
impact: Not a byte-identical copy of the official fp32 release.

what: B uses microbatch 1 x accumulation 4 instead of the official effective batch 8.
impact: Not claimed as bitwise reproduction of the paper.

what: L/D/A use 2000 updates, the official launch-script value; the paper reports about 3000.
impact: Disclosed in the report; no post-hoc checkpoint selection.

what: The engineering check used the untrained cross-initialized condition (parent_step 0), not B320.
why: Check only shapes/gradients/memory before paying for 8 baselines.
impact: No method-effect evidence is taken from engineering outputs.

what: Extra old-project image ids were audited after selection; overlap with the selected persons was empty.
why: The protocol's 12 ids were applied before selection; the old processed directory contained additional ids.
impact: No reselection needed; data/disen_formal/history_audit.json records the check.

what: Two launchers briefly started the same L/D/A jobs because an automatic chained launcher overlapped with a manual one.
why: Operational mistake in process supervision, not a method change.
impact: All L/D/A outputs from the affected few minutes were deleted before any result inspection; the 24 jobs were restarted once from clean directories. B outputs were unaffected.

what: After the freeze, only analysis/inference-support code changed: bf16-safe tensor hashing, a generate --image-ids filter for smoke tests/targeted regeneration, and report/aggregate scripts.
why: These are logging/tooling fixes; no training loss, optimizer, data, or model computation changed.
impact: The formal training runs were not restarted; the freeze's training-math assets still apply.

what: The repeat tasks' key swapped method labels unconditionally while images swapped  probabilistically; 11 of 16 repeat keys disagreed with the HTML images.
why: The original blind builder had a branch bug; an audit found it before final scoring.
impact: The key was repaired from the HTML image paths; task ids, page order and images were not changed, so already-entered A/B preference answers remain usable. The 160 original pairs were unaffected.

what: The first human aggregator used position 'A' as a fixed method, ignored identity_preference, mixed repeats into effects, mixed p01/p02 into edit rates and did not deduplicate images.
why: It did not implement the pre-registered human analysis semantics.
impact: Rewritten: 160 originals for effects, 16 repeats only for consistency; method labels from the key; image-level dedupe with conflicts; p03-p08 seed101 48/group edit guardrail; per-person bootstrap; partial ratings are not marked available.

what: Source selection joined identity_CelebA.txt with the mapping's zero-based orig_idx, while official filenames are one-based (orig_file).
why: The mapping exposes both idx/orig_idx and orig_file; the original code used the wrong column.
impact: All recorded person_ids were shifted. Recomputing with orig_file leaves the 10 selected sources 10 distinct people and empty overlap with corrected historical persons; no pixels, weights or ArcFace scores changed, so no retraining. identities.json and the audit were corrected.

what: The both-target and area-matched ArcFace subsets are 100/128 and 40/128 pairs (3-8 per person).
why: They are screened after generation, not randomised subsets.
impact: Reported as auxiliary, with counts; they do not replace the all-128 missing-face=0 primary metric.

what: The adapter comment/report called the +0.001 cosine term an alignment term.
why: Actually minimising a positive cosine pushes c and u apart.
impact: Comments and report corrected to a disentanglement/contrast term; the trained weights and loss sign were not changed.

what: B calls backward() on each of the 4 micro-batch losses without dividing by accumulation.
why: The custom trainer does not use Accelerator's automatic loss scaling.
impact: The gradient is a sum rather than an average. AdamW's moment normalisation largely cancels constant scaling, but this is disclosed; no retraining and no claim of a 4x effective LR.

what: The engineering checkpoint test saves toy tensors and an optimizer without trained moments.
why: It tests file/RNG round-trip, not real LoRA+adapter resume equivalence.
impact: Report wording narrowed; reliable resume of a real interrupted adaptation job is not claimed.

what: The eight prompts are fixed common edit prompts; some scenes overlap earlier experiments.
why: The new element is the people and the training method, not unseen prompt families.
impact: No claim of generalization to unseen scene families.
